# Navigation accuracy tuning reference

*Last comprehensively checked against the live `nav2_params.yaml`/BT XML: 2026-08-31. Individual
rows carry their own dates - if a row's date is old, verify its "Current" value against the yaml
directly rather than trusting it, the same way this pass found several stale values (§2's
`offset_from_furthest`, §5's AMCL `alpha`/`update_min_*`, §4's `smooth_path` claim) that had
silently drifted since this doc's previous update (2026-07-20).*

Parameters worth adjusting if Nav2 goal-reaching accuracy needs improvement, organized by
layer. See `CHANGELOG.md` / the 2026-07-13 fixes for the bugs already root-caused and fixed in
this stack (wheel collision shape, friction, steering PID gain) before this list was compiled -
this doc assumes those are already applied.

## Known mismatches (fixed)

- ~~Costmap footprint is a circle~~ **Fixed 2026-07-14 (11)**: `local_costmap`/`global_costmap`
  now use a real polygon `footprint`, measured directly from `models/qcar/QCarBody.stl` (0.409m
  long x 0.156m wide, rounded outward with a small margin) instead of `robot_radius: 0.15`. This
  became directly load-bearing once `CostCritic.consider_footprint: true` was enabled in §2 below
  - footprint-aware collision checking against an undersized circle wouldn't have actually
    protected the car's real front/rear overhangs.

## 1. Physics / drive plugin - `urdf/qcar_model.xacro` (`gazebo_ros_ackermann_drive` block, ~line 305)

**`/joint_states` fixed 2026-07-18 (8) - was fake/static, not read from physics.**
`gazebo_ros_ackermann_drive` does not publish `sensor_msgs/JointState` (verified against its
source); the only thing that used to publish `/joint_states` was the standalone
`joint_state_publisher` node in `launch/qcar_updated.launch.py`, which has no hardware feedback
and just emits a static all-zero position for every joint forever. That made RViz's rendered
wheels/steering look permanently frozen (and initially fooled this investigation too) even when
the vehicle was physically steering correctly - confirmed by reading the real `base`->`hubfl` TF
published by the drive plugin itself, which showed the hub angle moving normally. Fixed by adding
a `libgazebo_ros_joint_state_publisher.so` Gazebo plugin (reads real physics) and removing the
standalone node. See `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-18 (8) for the full investigation - including that
this was a real bug but does **not** fully explain the separate, still-open MPPI local-optimum
issue where the controller itself doesn't sustain commanded turns for some goal shapes.

| Param | Current | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `left/right_steering_pid_gain` | `3.0 0 0.1` | How well actual steer angle tracks commanded. Too low -> undershoot; too high -> oscillation/instability. |
| `linear_velocity_pid_gain` | `0.3 0 0.005` | Wheel-speed tracking accuracy - same trade-off. |
| Wheel collision `radius` (~line 142) | `0.036` | Feeds the plugin's `wheel_radius_` used to convert wheel spin -> odom linear velocity. A mismatch creates a **systematic odometry scale error** that accumulates over a whole path (padded +3mm over the mesh's true 0.033m for ground contact - worth testing a smaller pad if traction is solid). |
| `mu1`/`mu2` on wheels | `1.0` | Traction. Lower -> more slip/skid (less accurate); unrealistically high can cause its own instability. |
| `max_steer` | `0.5236` (30°) | Real hardware limit -> sets true min turning radius (~0.45m). Nav2's planner doesn't know this limit, so paths can ask for tighter turns than physically possible. |
| Wheel inertia (`ixx/iyy/izz`) | `0.0012/0.0022/0.0012` | Too low -> numerically unstable at higher PID gains (hit an `Ogre::AxisAlignedBox` crash once at the old, tinier value); too high -> sluggish response. |

## 2. Path following - `FollowPath` / MPPIController - `config/nav2/nav2_params.yaml:148`

As of 2026-07-14 (9) this is `nav2_mppi_controller::MPPIController`, not
`RegulatedPurePursuitController`. History: RPP was tuned extensively (lookahead distances, speed
regulation, replanning rate, `progress_checker` patience) trying to stabilize its handling of
path cusps (reverse/direction-change points) for goals needing a large final-heading change with
`allow_reversing: true`. It never became reliable - one goal would succeed, a geometrically
similar one would fail after 7+ minutes of retries. RPP's specific failure mode is tied to its
lookahead-point ("carrot point") pure-pursuit geometry, which has no robust handling for a large
lookahead radius straddling both sides of a cusp. MPPI is architecturally different: each control
cycle it samples many candidate trajectories and scores them against cost critics, rather than
tracking one lookahead point - it doesn't have RPP's specific failure mode, and natively supports
an Ackermann motion model with a real minimum-turning-radius constraint (verified via
`/opt/ros/humble/include/nav2_mppi_controller/motion_models.hpp`).

**Only structural parameters are set explicitly** (motion model, velocity limits, turning radius,
which critics to load) - per-critic cost weights are left at nav2's own built-in defaults, since
this package doesn't have local access to the critics' `.cpp` source to verify non-default weight
values with confidence. Retune individual critic weights only after testing these defaults live.

| Param | Current | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `motion_model` | `"Ackermann"` | Selects `AckermannMotionModel`, which enforces `AckermannConstraints.min_turning_r` as a hard constraint on sampled trajectories (verified string present in the compiled `.so` and declared in the header). |
| `AckermannConstraints.min_turning_r` | `0.5` m | This vehicle's true hard turning-radius limit. As of 2026-07-19 (2), **deliberately NOT kept equal** to `planner_server.GridBased.minimum_turning_radius` below anymore - see that row for why keeping them in sync (the original guidance here) turned out to cause a real freeze. |
| `vx_max` / `vx_min` | `0.3` / `-0.2` | Forward/reverse speed limits. Reverse magnitude kept lower than forward since the drive plugin's PID (`urdf/qcar_model.xacro`, see §1) was only tuned/verified for forward speeds up to 0.3 m/s. |
| `vx_std` / `wz_std` | `0.2` / `0.4` (plugin defaults) | Lowered to `0.15`/`0.3` on 2026-07-18 after the user shared video evidence of mid-trip path deviation - tighter sampling = less wobble, and live-tested well at the time (max path deviation `0.447m -> 0.375m`, final accuracy `0.139m -> 0.054m`, at the cost of total travel time `122s -> 172s`). **Reverted back to the defaults on 2026-07-19 (2)**: live-testing a goal requiring a long, tight-radius approach found the tightened noise made a *different* bug much worse - MPPI samples each cycle's candidates as noise added to the previous cycle's control sequence (`Optimizer::shiftControlSequence()`), so once that sequence collapsed toward near-zero velocity, tighter noise made it measurably harder to sample anything far enough from "near zero" to escape, and the robot stayed frozen until a recovery behavior forced a full `Optimizer::reset()`. If wobble reappears without this freeze, prefer tuning `PathAlignCritic`/`PathFollowCritic` weights over re-tightening these - see `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-19 (2). |
| `iteration_count` | `2` | Raised from `1` on 2026-07-19 (2), alongside the sampling-noise revert above - a second optimization pass per control cycle lets MPPI refine away from a bad warm-started sequence within the same cycle instead of relying on next-cycle sampling luck. Doubles per-cycle optimizer CPU cost; live-verified to still complete within the 50ms `controller_frequency` budget, though it produces occasional "Control loop missed its desired rate" warnings under load - reduce `batch_size` first if that becomes a real problem. |
| `vy_max` / `vy_std` | `0.0` | Zero - this is a non-holonomic vehicle, no lateral motion. |
| `wz_max` | `1.9` | Max angular velocity considered during sampling. |
| `batch_size` / `time_steps` / `model_dt` | `2000` / `56` / `0.05` | Core MPPI sampling parameters - more samples/longer horizon = better trajectory quality but more CPU per control cycle. Reduce `batch_size` first if `controller_frequency: 20.0` (above) starts getting missed under load. Raising `batch_size` (to `2500`/`3500`) was live-tested on 2026-07-19 (4) as a fix for path-tracking looseness (see `PathAlignCritic.cost_weight` row above for the failed critic-weight attempt at the same problem) - it genuinely worked for that (p90 plan-deviation `0.33-0.41m -> 0.25-0.26m`, 2 trials each, reproducible), but the extra CPU cost degraded control-loop timing enough near the goal that one otherwise-normal run took **4.5 minutes** to converge instead of ~30s. Reverted - see `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-19 (4) for the full trial data if revisiting this. |
| `enforce_path_inversion` | `true` | **Critical for this vehicle.** MPPI has dedicated logic for a path containing a cusp/reversal (as `SmacPlannerHybrid`'s Reeds-Shepp K-turns produce) - without this, it defaults to `false` and does not correctly treat the path as "drive to the cusp, then continue past it." Confirmed (after the initial MPPI switch) to be the actual cause of the robot not following the planned path at all, not a critic-weight issue - see `CHANGELOG.md`'s 2026-07-14 (10) entry. If reversing is ever disabled again (`vx_min >= 0`, `motion_model_for_search: "DUBIN"`), this can safely go back to `false` since there'd be no cusps to handle. |
| `inversion_xy_tolerance` / `inversion_yaw_tolerance` | `0.2` m / `0.4` rad (~23°) | Position/heading window within which the robot is considered to have reached the cusp, so MPPI advances to the path segment beyond it. Tighter values demand a more precise stop at the cusp before continuing (more correct-looking but slower); looser values move on sooner (faster but the "K-turn" may look less clean). Widening to `0.4`/`0.7` was tried 2026-08-25 as a fix for the mid-route cusp freeze (see below) - **worse** (repeated `progress_checker` aborts before even reaching the cusp) - reverted to stock. The freeze was fixed instead via the `cusp_straightener` smoother, §2a below, which reshapes the path so it naturally converges within these stock tolerances rather than needing them loosened. |
| `critics` | `["ConstraintCritic", "CostCritic", "GoalCritic", "GoalAngleCritic", "PathAlignCritic", "PathFollowCritic", "PathAngleCritic", "EarlyCommitCritic"]` | Which cost functions score each candidate trajectory. `EarlyCommitCritic` (custom, this package) added 2026-07-18 (9), see its own row below. `PreferForwardCritic` was **removed** 2026-07-15 (3) - its source (fetched from GitHub, not guessed) showed it penalizes any reverse velocity for as long as the robot is >0.5m from goal, while `PathFollowCritic` (before its own fix below) stopped enforcing the plan inside 1.4m - the 0.5-1.4m gap let `PreferForwardCritic` actively fight a planned reversal with nothing defending it. Live-tested: fixed a K-turn goal that previously failed catastrophically (2.2m/177deg error) down to 0.145m/0.22deg. Default `cost_weight`s of the remaining critics, verified directly against the Humble source (`nav2_mppi_controller/src/critics/*.cpp` on GitHub): `ConstraintCritic` 4.0, `CostCritic` 3.81, `GoalCritic` 5.0, `GoalAngleCritic` 3.0, `PathAlignCritic` 10.0, `PathFollowCritic` 5.0, `PathAngleCritic` 2.0. A custom `PathDeviationCritic` (`src/critics/path_deviation_critic.cpp`, "don't insist on exact path rejoin when deviated, aim further ahead instead") was implemented and trial-tested 2026-08-26 - regressed timing (mean 74.3s vs the active config's 43.9s, much wider variance) - reverted, not in the active list, code kept deselected. |
| `CostCritic.consider_footprint` | `true` | Defaults to **false** - was a real bug in the original MPPI config (docs claimed `true`, the yaml never set it), meaning collision/obstacle cost was evaluated at the robot's center point only, not its actual elongated footprint. A plausible direct cause of corner-cutting near obstacles. **Depends on the costmap's own footprint being accurate** - see the circular-footprint mismatch flagged at the top of this doc; footprint-aware collision checking against an undersized circular approximation won't fully protect the car's real overhangs. |
| `GoalCritic.cost_weight` | `8.0` | Raised from the default `5.0` - final position was reported inaccurate even when nav2 considered the goal "reached." Live-tested alongside the `PreferForwardCritic` removal - contributed to convergence within 0.14-0.20m across two test goals (down from >0.6m before both fixes). |
| `GoalAngleCritic.cost_weight` | `10.0` | Raised from the default `3.0` on 2026-07-18 (5) - fixes the robot not moving on a new goal that's mainly a reorientation (same/near position, new final yaw). Root cause: `PathAlignCritic`/`PathFollowCritic`/`PathAngleCritic`'s `threshold_to_consider` gates on distance from the robot's **current** pose to the goal (`utils::withinPositionGoalTolerance`), which is ~0 for this scenario from the first control cycle - disabling all three for the entire maneuver, leaving `GoalAngleCritic` as the only active guidance against `ConstraintCritic`'s turning-radius penalty. Live-tested: measurably improves recovery (often converges directly, otherwise unstuck by `progress_checker`'s retry loop within ~30-90s) with no regression on normal short goals (~5-11s, same as baseline). **Not a complete fix** - still occasionally fails outright on retry-budget exhaustion in live testing, since MPPI's sampling is stochastic and the underlying critic-gating gap is unchanged. `30.0` converges faster/more directly but was live-verified to regress a separate normal goal's final approach - reverted. See `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-18 (5). |
| `PathFollowCritic.threshold_to_consider` / `PathAlignCritic.threshold_to_consider` | `0.15` | Lowered from the defaults `1.4` / `0.5` - closes the "dead zone" described above so path-following guidance stays active closer to the final approach. **Does not fix** the reorientation-in-place bug described in the `GoalAngleCritic` row above - live-verified to have zero effect on that case, since the gate is based on current-position-to-goal distance, which is already ~0 for that scenario regardless of this value. |
| `PathFollowCritic.offset_from_furthest` / `PathAngleCritic.offset_from_furthest` | `6` / `4` (defaults, explicit) | Lowered to `3` / `2` on 2026-07-18 (2) after the user reported (and shared video of) the robot turning early, before an upcoming curve in the planned path actually starts - confirmed via the real scoring code (`path_follow_critic.cpp` / `path_angle_critic.cpp` on GitHub) that both critics target a path point this many *indices* ahead of the robot's current furthest-reached progress, and a target that far ahead can land past the start of a curve, pulling the executed heading toward it prematurely. Re-tested 2026-08-02 against the defaults (`6`/`4`) and a much wider `36`/`24` on a different, harder reorientation goal as part of a 5-parameter investigation - "no meaningful change at either value" on that goal. **Live config is currently back at the defaults (`6`/`4`)** - no changelog entry explicitly documents reverting from `3`/`2`, so treat this as a real, currently-unexplained discrepancy from the 2026-07-18 (2) value rather than a confirmed deliberate decision; re-verify against the original "turning early" symptom before trusting either value blindly. |
| `PathAlignCritic.offset_from_furthest` | `3` | Lowered from the default `20` on 2026-07-18 (3), after the fix above alone didn't resolve the reported symptom. Works completely differently here than in the other two critics - it's a **gate**, not a look-ahead target (`path_align_critic.cpp`): `PathAlignCritic` (the highest-weighted critic in use, at `10.0`) is entirely inactive for the first `offset_from_furthest` path points of every trip. At the default `20`, the strongest path-adherence critic simply wasn't running yet for an early curve. Live-tested on the same isolated forward-curve goal as the fix above: max path deviation tightened `0.123m -> 0.091m -> 0.083m` across the two fix rounds, with every sampled point staying under 9cm from the path. **User-confirmed fixed** against real RViz recordings (the green line in both shared videos was the actual `/plan` topic) - see `CHANGELOG.md`'s 2026-07-18 (3) entry. |
| `PathAlignCritic.cost_weight` | `10.0` (default, left explicit) | Investigated 2026-07-19 (3) after "robot doesn't turn as much as the planned curve" was reported following the `vx_std`/`wz_std` restoration above - live-confirmed real corner-cutting (~0.15m inside the planned arc at a comparable point). Tried `14.0` (worse: overshot the *other* way, `x~0.84-0.89` vs planned `~0.49`, then stalled oscillating) and `12.0` (same overshoot numbers as `14.0`, not a graded response). A dense-sampled control run back at the `10.0` default swung *even wider* (`x~1.11`) on a different run of the identical goal/config - run-to-run MPPI stochasticity at this wider sampling is large enough that a single-run weight experiment isn't reliable evidence. Left at the default rather than commit to an untested value; see `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-19 (3) for the full investigation and what a more rigorous follow-up would need (multiple trials per candidate weight). |
| `EarlyCommitCritic` (custom, `src/critics/early_commit_critic.cpp`) | `offset_from_furthest: 3`, `early_time_steps: 10`, `active_path_points: 8`, `forward_preference: false`, `cost_weight: 15.0` | Added 2026-07-18 (9) - **not a stock nav2 critic**, defined in this package. Fixes a case no amount of tuning the stock critics above could reach: a goal whose path curves immediately from the robot's current position (stock `PathAngleCritic` is gated by `max_angle_to_furthest`, ~69deg by default, so it provides zero heading guidance for moderate initial mismatches). Scores only the first `early_time_steps` of each sampled trajectory against the bearing to a near-term path point, unconditionally - no `threshold_to_consider`/`max_angle_to_furthest` gate - but only while `active_path_points` hasn't been exceeded, so it steps aside for the rest of a normal trip (live-tested without that gate: fixed the stuck-at-start case but broke ordinary path-following everywhere else). See `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-18 (9) for the full investigation, including a real ABI-mismatch crash (missing `XTENSOR_USE_XSIMD` define, must match `nav2_mppi_controller`'s own `CMakeLists.txt` exactly) that had to be fixed first. `forward_preference: false` added 2026-07-19 (1) - the same freeze recurred later in a trip whenever `SmacPlannerHybrid` planned a Reeds-Shepp reverse (K-turn) segment: the critic originally assumed forward-only travel and scored the correct reverse maneuver as ~180deg wrong, fighting it. Now scores yaw against whichever of (bearing, bearing+180deg) is closer - `nav2_mppi_controller`'s own `utils::posePointAngle()` reversing convention - letting `ConstraintCritic`/`PathFollowCritic`/etc. decide whether forward or reverse is actually cheaper. Live-confirmed via a `/plan` dump mid-stall (a 3-pose reverse segment right where the robot froze) and a before/after retest of the same reproduction goal: frozen indefinitely -> `Reached the goal!`/`Goal succeeded` within ~10s. See `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-19 (1). `active_path_points` lowered from `15` to `8` on 2026-07-19 (5) after a safety-relevant report: the robot turning before the planned curve starts, deviating enough to risk hitting obstacles. Root cause on a goal whose path runs straight for ~1m before curving: the curve happened to start around path point 15-16, squarely inside the (then) 15-point active window, so this highest-weighted, ungated critic kept reaching toward the upcoming curve well before the vehicle got there (live-measured: actual lateral position up to 3x the planned value at matching points along the straight section). Lowering to `8` measurably reduced this (down to ~1.9x at the same comparison point) without regressing the original curve-at-trip-start case (`(0.6, 0.8, 90deg)` retested, still succeeds cleanly). Not a full fix - `PathFollowCritic`/`PathAngleCritic`'s own look-ahead offsets below aren't gated by `active_path_points` and likely account for the remainder; see `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-19 (5) for the next lever if this resurfaces. |

If MPPI still doesn't reliably handle reversing near a goal after `enforce_path_inversion: true`,
that would indicate the problem is genuinely in the planned path (SmacPlannerHybrid, §4) rather
than the controller - a good diagnostic split RPP couldn't offer, since RPP's own instability was
always a confound.

**RESOLVED 2026-08-26, see §2a below.** First confirmed 2026-07-18 (6): a path with a
reverse-then-forward (cusp) segment could get the robot stuck in a `Failed to make progress` /
replan loop at the cusp, root-caused to `path_handler.cpp`'s `isWithinInversionTolerances`
requiring a precise simultaneous position+heading match before the path beyond the cusp is
revealed. Widening `inversion_xy_tolerance`/`inversion_yaw_tolerance` (tested again 2026-08-25,
`0.2/0.4 -> 0.4/0.7`) was **worse** (repeated `progress_checker` aborts before even reaching the
cusp) - reverted, still at the stock `0.2`m / `0.4`rad. The actual fix that worked was a custom
path-smoother plugin that reshapes the path *before* MPPI ever sees it, rather than loosening
MPPI's own gating - see §2a.

**Related but distinct fix, 2026-07-19 (2): blind periodic replanning at the BT level.**
`config/nav2/behavior_trees/*.xml` used to replan on a fixed timer regardless of whether the
current path was still fine - lowered from stock nav2's 1Hz to 0.2Hz on 2026-07-15 as a partial
mitigation, but a long/demanding goal could still get torn up every 5s before completing a
maneuver. Rewrote both trees to replan only when `IsPathValid` actually fails or the goal changes,
with an unconditional one-time initial plan (a plain `<Sequence>`, not nav2_behavior_tree's
`SingleTrigger` - a first attempt at that caused ~33Hz unconditional replanning, see
`CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-19 (2) for exactly why) to avoid the empty-path/`IsPathValid` bug that
blocked this approach the first time it was tried. Live-verified: zero unwanted `/plan`
republishes across a 30s+ window. This is a genuine, separate fix from the mid-route-cusp bug
above - both concern replanning, but this one is about *how often* a still-valid path gets
needlessly discarded, not about cusp/inversion handling specifically.

**`IsPathValidDebounced` (custom BT condition, tried and reverted 2026-08-26).** A debounced
replacement for stock `IsPathValid` (require N consecutive invalid checks before replanning,
absorbing single-tick blips) - worked well in sim and on an initial hardware goal, but on a later
hardware run a *persistently* (not transiently) invalid path caused continuous replan/abort
cycling that never let `FollowPath` hold a plan long enough to execute a reverse segment. Root
cause suspected to be an uncorrected clock offset between the dev PC and the QCar (scan/odom
timestamp mismatch misplacing obstacles in the local costmap), not a flaw in the debounce logic
itself, but reverted to stock `IsPathValid` rather than keep debugging live ahead of a demo. Code
kept (`src/bt/is_path_valid_debounced_condition.cpp`), not wired into the BT. See `CHANGELOG.md`
2026-08-26 and the `qcar_updated_mppi_cusp_freeze_investigation` memory before re-enabling.

## 2a. Path smoothing - `smoother_server` / custom `cusp_straightener` - `nav2_params.yaml:405`, `behavior_trees/*.xml`

**This is new since this doc was last updated (2026-07-20) and is the actual fix for the
mid-route-cusp freeze described in §2 above.** As of 2026-08-25, both `<ComputePathToPose>` call
sites in `navigate_to_pose_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml` are followed by
`<SmoothPath smoother_id="cusp_straightener">`, so `smoother_server` is genuinely in the loop now
- this contradicts the older claim under §4's `smooth_path` row that the planner's own internal
smoothing is "the only smoothing actually applied." It isn't anymore.

A front-steered vehicle's steered wheels are the self-correcting leading axle going forward but
the jackknife-prone trailing axle in reverse - curving immediately from a standing start in
reverse is the hardest sub-case of a K-turn, and this is what was actually driving the MPPI freeze
at cusps (not cusp count, not steering calibration, both tested and ruled out first). The custom
`CuspStraightenerSmoother` plugin (`src/smoothers/cusp_straightener_smoother.cpp`) re-shapes the
path *before* MPPI ever sees it, rather than loosening MPPI's own inversion-tolerance gating (that
approach was tried, see §2's inversion tolerance history, and was worse).

| Param | Current | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `straight_distance` | `0.21` m | At each REVERSE-entering cusp, re-projects this much arc length onto a straight line continuing the cusp's heading, blending back to the original curve over the same distance - gives the vehicle a straight run to start reversing on instead of curving immediately. 3-vs-3-vs-3 trial: baseline (no smoother) mean 110.2s/2 recoveries -> this alone mean 86.7s/1.3 recoveries. |
| `extend_distance` | `0.15` m | Also pushes the cusp point itself this much further before the straight/reverse leg starts, so the incoming and outgoing legs overlap/cross instead of meeting at one precise vertex - widens MPPI's cusp-arrival target (`inversion_xy/yaw_tolerance` in §2 need to converge on that vertex exactly). Combined with `straight_distance`: mean 43.9s/0 recoveries across 3 trials - the final locked-in config, hardware-validated (2/2 goals, 0 recoveries). As of 2026-08-29, the extension continues the incoming path's own curvature (estimated over a ~0.15m lookback window) instead of cutting straight - a first attempt at this used only the single adjacent path segment, which the planner's `angle_quantization_bins: 72` (5deg steps) dominated with noise, producing an unrealistically tight extension curve that made the robot deviate off-path and get stuck; fixed by widening the curvature estimate's lookback window. Sim-verified (0 `Failed to make progress` vs 2 before, 37s vs 99s on the reproduction goal), **not yet hardware-tested**. |
| `min_lead_distance` | `0.3` m | Added 2026-08-29: a replanned path starts at the robot's live pose, so the same physical cusp kept reappearing near the front of the path and getting re-extended on every replan while the robot was still approaching/executing it - by the time it was essentially already there (very small remaining lead distance), re-extending just reshaped the path under the robot each tick instead of a one-time approach adjustment. Only applies extend+straighten when the cusp is still at least this far ahead; skips (no treatment at all) once the robot is essentially already at/into it. Sim-verified firing correctly, not yet hardware-tested. |

`simple_smoother` (stock `nav2_smoother::SimpleSmoother`) is also configured in this block but
**not** wired into the BT (no `<SmoothPath>` call references it) - dead config, kept per this
project's own "don't remove dead config without a reason" convention (see the
`qcar_updated_dont_proactively_cleanup_dead_config` memory).

Full history (v1 hard-cutover regression, a multi-cusp corruption bug, the `extend_distance`
curvature bug and fix): `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-08-25/26/29 and the
`qcar_updated_mppi_cusp_freeze_investigation` memory.

## 3. Goal checker - `nav2_params.yaml:127`

| Param | Current | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `xy_goal_tolerance` | `0.12` | Widened slightly from `0.1` on 2026-07-15 (3) - a live-tested K-turn goal converged to 0.145m and cycled through repeated abort/retries instead of latching "reached" at the old, stricter tolerance. Tighter = more accurate stop, but harder to satisfy (may cause hunting/oscillation near the goal for a car that can't easily fine-adjust position). |
| `yaw_goal_tolerance` | `0.5` (~29°) | Final heading matters for this deployment (confirmed by the user) - the original guidance here was not to loosen this drastically to mask goal-approach oscillation. Widened `0.3` -> `0.5` on 2026-07-20 by the user's own hands-on tuning, but paired with `minimum_turning_radius` raised to `1.0` below, not as a standalone workaround - user-confirmed the pair reaches goals "almost accurately." See `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-20. |

## 4. Global planner - `GridBased` / SmacPlannerHybrid - `nav2_params.yaml:190`

As of 2026-07-14 this is `nav2_smac_planner/SmacPlannerHybrid`, not the original
`nav2_navfn_planner/NavfnPlanner` - switched because `NavfnPlanner` is curvature- and
heading-agnostic (plans paths with turns tighter than the car can physically execute, and has no
concept of arrival orientation at all), which was the root cause of a goal-approach oscillation
where `RegulatedPurePursuitController` kept trying to improvise a final-heading correction
reactively. See `CHANGELOG.md`'s 2026-07-14 entries for the full diagnosis history.

**`motion_model_for_search` is `"REEDS_SHEPP"` (reversing allowed).** History: this was the
original choice, found unstable when paired with `RegulatedPurePursuitController` (RPP doesn't
handle path cusps robustly in this Humble nav2 version - confirmed via live testing), switched to
`"DUBIN"` (forward-only, no cusps) as a stable workaround, then switched back once the local
controller itself was replaced with MPPI (§2 above).

**Correction (2026-07-18 (6)/(7)): MPPI is not immune to this either.** The line that used to be
here claimed MPPI's trajectory-sampling approach doesn't share RPP's cusp failure mode - that
turned out to be wrong, just live-verified too late to have caught it earlier. MPPI has its own,
differently-shaped fragility around cusps/reversals: (6) found the robot can get stuck in a
`Failed to make progress` / replan loop at a mid-route cusp (root cause traced to
`PathHandler::isWithinInversionTolerances` in `nav2_mppi_controller`, requiring the robot to
simultaneously satisfy both a position and yaw tolerance before the rest of the path is released -
**resolved 2026-08-26 via the `cusp_straightener` path smoother, §2a**, not by touching MPPI's own
tolerances); (7) found `SmacPlannerHybrid` inserting a small, unnecessary reversal as literally
the *first* segment of many plans (fixed via `change_penalty` below, but see that fix's own
caveat about pushing large-heading-change goals toward long forward-only loops instead). Treat
`"REEDS_SHEPP"` as still generally worth care around cusps/reversals in this stack even with both
fixes in place. `reverse_penalty` (below) is raised to prefer forward-only routes when possible,
both to minimize unnecessary reversing and because reversal segments are where this fragility
concentrates.

| Param | Current | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `motion_model_for_search` | `"REEDS_SHEPP"` | Allows reverse/K-turn segments in the planned path. `"DUBIN"` (forward-only, no cusps) remains the fallback if instability somehow returns with MPPI too - see the history above and in `CHANGELOG.md`. |
| `minimum_turning_radius` | `1.0` m | Padded over the car's true ~0.445m minimum (wheelbase / tan(max steer)). Raised from `0.5` to `0.7` on 2026-07-19 (2) - `0.5` exactly matched `FollowPath.AckermannConstraints.min_turning_r` (the controller's own hard limit), which left MPPI's sampled trajectories zero margin: any sample noisier than perfect curves slightly tighter than 0.5m and gets penalized, so MPPI kept preferring straighter, cheaper trajectories over actually committing to a tight required curve - live-confirmed via a circle fit on a real `/plan` dump (fitted radius `0.49999999m`) that the robot froze on. Raised further to `1.0` by the user's own hands-on tuning on 2026-07-20, paired with `general_goal_checker.yaw_goal_tolerance` widened to `0.5` (§3) - user-confirmed the pair reaches goals "almost accurately." Important: `1.0` tested *alone* (yaw tolerance still `0.3`) previously measured worse than `0.7` on a K-turn goal (wider swing, same reversal pattern) - see `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-20 for why the pairing behaves differently and why these two should be changed together. Lower cautiously, and re-check this margin, if `max_steer`/the steering PID is later retuned to allow tighter turns. |
| `reverse_penalty` | `4.0` | Raised from `2.0` - makes the planner prefer a forward-only route even if longer, only actually planning a reverse segment when the goal orientation truly can't be reached forward-only. Fewer cusps encountered in practice = fewer chances to hit the residual instability. Raise further if oscillation returns and you'd rather the car take a longer forward route than reverse at all in most cases. |
| `non_straight_penalty` | `1.2` | Discourages unnecessary curvature in the planned path, for smoother routes. |
| `change_penalty` | `3.0` | Raised from the default `0.0` on 2026-07-18 (7). `node_hybrid.cpp`'s own comment on this term: "penalizes wiggling" - applied when consecutive motion primitives switch turning direction. At `0.0` (nav2's real default, not a prior misconfiguration here) there's no cost at all for the planner inserting a short, unnecessary direction-changing segment - live-confirmed this was happening as literally the *first* segment of many plans (a small reversal immediately followed by forward motion) whenever the robot's start heading didn't already match the path's initial tangent, which was the actual cause of a reported "doesn't move when the path starts with a turn" bug - not an MPPI/controller tuning issue. Live-verified fix for that specific symptom; see `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-18 (7) for the new trade-off this surfaced (large-heading-change goals now sometimes take a long forward-only loop instead of a short reverse, combined with `reverse_penalty` below - not yet resolved). |
| `cost_penalty` | `2.0` | Weight on costmap cost in the search - higher pushes the path further from inflated obstacle zones. |
| `smooth_path` | `true` | Planner's own internal path smoothing. **As of 2026-08-25 this is NOT the only smoothing applied anymore** - `smoother_server`'s custom `cusp_straightener` plugin also runs, via an explicit `<SmoothPath>` call in the BT (see §2a) - that older claim was wrong even before this doc's own last update, and has been wrong since. |
| `max_planning_time` | `5.0` s | Hard cap per planning attempt - Hybrid-A* is more expensive than NavfnPlanner's Dijkstra/A*, worth watching if replanning starts feeling sluggish on a larger map. Confirmed live (2026-08-29) it's `max_iterations` that actually gets hit on a hard/infeasible goal (each failed attempt takes 2.5-3.6s, well under this 5.0s cap), not this time budget - see the `max_iterations`/`tolerance` row below. |
| `angle_quantization_bins` | `72` | Heading resolution of the search space (5 deg per bin) - finer bins = more precise final heading but slower search. Also the source of a real bug found 2026-08-29: this coarse quantization dominated a single-adjacent-segment curvature *estimate* used by the `cusp_straightener` smoother's `extend_distance`, producing an unrealistically tight extension curve - see §2a, `extend_distance` row. |
| `max_iterations` / `tolerance` | `1000000` / `0.5` | `SmacPlannerHybrid`'s search loop exits when either the queue empties or `max_iterations` is hit; on either exit it backtracks to the closest node reached within `tolerance` of the goal instead of failing outright, if one was found (confirmed against the real `a_star.cpp` search loop, humble branch, not guessed). Practical effect: a goal within collision-checking range of an obstacle (e.g. `< tolerance` clearance for this vehicle's footprint) can exhaust `max_iterations` searching for a full-footprint-valid pose that doesn't exist there, and fail with `exceeded maximum iterations` - **this is a goal-placement problem, not a config bug**; check clearance at the goal (map resolution/origin vs. footprint half-length) before assuming a regression. `tolerance` was tried at `1.0` (from `0.5`) on 2026-08-29 specifically to rescue such a near-wall goal, and it worked - but the "rescued" pose becomes the plan's actual endpoint, and nothing downstream rechecks it against the originally-requested goal, so the robot could end up meaningfully far from where it was actually sent and still report `Goal succeeded`. **Reverted to `0.5`** - a visible failure on an unreachable goal is preferable to a silent wrong-pose success for this project (see the `qcar_updated_prefer_visible_failure_over_silent_wrong_result` memory). If a genuinely-needed goal is this tight, fix the real clearance there instead of widening this. |

If cusp/reversing behavior is still unreliable after the MPPI switch (§2), that now points at the
planned path itself rather than path-following - inspect `/plan` during a large-heading-change
goal to check whether `SmacPlannerHybrid` is producing a sane K-turn geometry, before assuming
it's a controller problem again.

## 5. AMCL - `nav2_params.yaml:10-44`

`robot_model_type: "nav2_amcl::DifferentialMotionModel"` (line 35) is correct as-is and does
**not** need to change. Checked directly against the `nav2_amcl` source
(`/opt/ros/humble/include/nav2_amcl/motion_model/*.hpp`): both shipped motion models
(`DifferentialMotionModel`, `OmniMotionModel`) consume the same raw odometry pose delta and the
same 5 `alpha` noise params - the model name doesn't refer to the vehicle's real drivetrain, it
refers to how the delta gets decomposed into particle noise. "Differential" = rotate-translate-
rotate, i.e. non-holonomic (can't move sideways without also turning/driving) - true for an
Ackermann car exactly as much as a diff-drive robot. "Omni" adds an explicit lateral *strafe*
noise term for robots that can genuinely move sideways (mecanum/omni wheels), which this car
cannot do - switching to it would inject particle-spread hypotheses for motion the robot can
never produce, which can hurt localization efficiency rather than help it. There is no
Ackermann-specific motion model in stock Nav2; `DifferentialMotionModel` is the standard choice
for any non-holonomic robot, car-like or not.

The actual accuracy levers here:

| Param | Current | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `alpha1-alpha5` | `0.4` each | Motion-model noise the filter expects per unit of travel/rotation. Raised from `0.2` (see `CHANGELOG.md` 2026-07-15 (2)) - live-measured map->odom TF jumps of up to 7cm/2.3deg in a single 0.2s step during goal-approach reorientation (K-turns with reversing), visible as lidar points "jumping" in the map frame each time AMCL corrected. Real wheel odometry drift during tight/reversing motion (more slip) was higher than `0.2` assumed, so AMCL underestimated uncertainty between scan-match updates and corrected in large, sudden jumps instead of tracking a wider, more realistic uncertainty gradually. If real odometry is noisier than this, particles under-spread and localization overconfidently drifts - raise further at the cost of noisier pose estimates. |
| `update_min_d` / `update_min_a` | `0.15` / `0.1` | How far the robot must move before AMCL re-localizes against the scan. Lowered from `0.25`/`0.2` alongside the `alpha` increase above (same `CHANGELOG.md` entry) - re-localizes more often with smaller corrections each time, rather than accumulating more drift between updates and correcting in one larger jump. Smaller = more frequent corrections (better accuracy, more CPU). |
| `laser_max_range`, `z_hit`, `z_rand`, `sigma_hit` | `12.0 / 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.2` | Scan-matching confidence model - `z_hit` vs `z_rand` balance affects how much AMCL trusts clean vs noisy lidar returns. |

## 6. Costmap - `nav2_params.yaml:187-269`

| Param | Current | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `inflation_radius` / `cost_scaling_factor` | `0.55 / 3.0` | Controls how far obstacles push the planned path away - directly shapes how tight a path the planner will attempt near walls. |
| `footprint` | `[[0.22,0.09],[0.22,-0.09],[-0.22,-0.09],[-0.22,0.09]]` | Real polygon matching the car's measured body extent, replacing the old `robot_radius: 0.15` circle as of 2026-07-14 (11) - see "Known mismatches" above. If this is ever revised (new mesh, added bumpers/sensors changing the real extent), remeasure from the STL rather than eyeballing it, and keep `local_costmap`/`global_costmap` in sync. |

## Suggested debugging order

1. Fix the footprint (cheap, structural, no physics retuning needed).
2. Watch whether errors concentrate at tight turns (-> tune `lookahead_dist` /
   `regulated_linear_scaling_min_radius`, or consider Smac Hybrid-A*) vs. general position drift
   over long paths (-> check AMCL `alpha` params and the wheel-radius odometry scale first).

## Open correction (found 2026-08-30, not yet applied to thesis)
Ch6's already-written "curvature-continuing" cusp-extension refinement (added earlier this
session) describes a two-point curvature estimate that the changelog shows was buggy — it made

34	- PPT 2026-05-25: LiDAR + Cartographer added, first map built. **Issue**: "Robot orientation not
35	  updating in RViz" — root cause named as QoS mismatch between `joint_state_broadcaster` and
36	  `robot_state_publisher`.
37	- PPT 2026-06-08: Nav2 launched (imprecise). **Issue**: robot pose static in RViz while moving in
38	  Gazebo — refined root cause: missing odom→base transform, since `drive_controller` never
39	  published odometry.
40	- **Status: partially in thesis** (end-state ground-truth-odom decision is in §3.2; the TF
41	  debugging itself is not narrated).
42	
43	## Phase 3 — `qcar_ackermann`: prototyping the Ackermann plugin (mid-June)
44	Built as a throwaway test package to prove dropping `ros2_control` for
45	`libgazebo_ros_ackermann_drive`, later merged back into `qcar_initial`. Bug chain, from the
46	chat-till-June-17 + parallel qcar_ackermann chat:
47	- Launch bugs: `robot_description` YAML parse error (`Command()` not typed as string), unreliable
48	  Gazebo launch pattern, spawn race condition.
49	- False lead: "robot spawned without wheels" — actually LiDAR ray-visualization obscuring the
50	  view, not a real defect.
51	- Dual actuation conflict — old and new drive plugins both active, fighting over `/cmd_vel`.
52	- Ackermann joint-mapping bug — wrong joint names, steering silently ignored.
53	- **LiDAR TF bug** — `continuous` joint with no `/joint_states` source, blocked all of Nav2.
54	  Likely the real cause of the broken-TF screenshots shown earlier in this conversation.
55	- Wheel-flip-on-joint-axis (different fix than the axis-negation already in the thesis for the
56	  ros2_control-based migration — same symptom class, different correct fix depending on consumer).
57	- PID gains entirely absent → zero torque → free drift (found by reading plugin source).
58	- Wheel vibration from concave mesh collision; fixing it unmasked missing joint damping.
59	- PID retuning needed because plugin demo defaults (`1500 0 1`) were tuned for a full-size car,
60	  not a 2.4kg QCar.
61	- **DDS `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` bug** — picking up another machine's ROS2 nodes over the network. Good
62	  concrete pairing for the DDS/SPDP discovery theory already in Ch2.
63	- Broken teleop script after the plugin switch.
64	- Wheel radius=0 bug — same defect signature as what's already in Table `tab:not-moving-bugs`
65	  bug #1, caught here mid-investigation.
66	- **Status: mostly not in thesis** — only the final wheel-radius/friction fix made it into the
67	  existing table.
68	
69	## Phase 4 — Package rename + first Nav2/MPPI maturation (July 2026)
70	- 2026-07-01 to 07-05 (git): `qcar_initial` → renamed to `qcar_updated`.
71	- 2026-07-05 (git/CHANGELOG): migrated JointGroup controllers → `ackermann_steering_controller`
72	  (**= thesis's First Migration, in thesis**).
73	- 2026-07-13 (git/CHANGELOG): migrated → `libgazebo_ros_ackermann_drive` directly, fixed
74	  "not moving"/"not reaching goal" (**= thesis's Second Migration + Table tab:not-moving-bugs,
75	  in thesis**).
76	
77	## Phase 5 — The goal-approach oscillation → planner/controller saga (2026-07-14, all one day)
78	**This is NOT a clean one-shot fix. It's an iterative arc that changed both the planner and the
79	controller, and even after 9+ rounds was not claimed as fully solved. Document it as an ongoing,
80	partially-resolved investigation, not a solved bug.**
81	
82	Starting symptom: robot reaches goal position but swings/wobbles correcting final orientation.
83	
84	1. Root cause: `NavfnPlanner` has no heading concept at all; default BT replans every second
85	   continuously, even after reaching goal position. Removed `<Spin>` recovery (physically
86	   impossible for this car) — **already in thesis, §sec:bt-fix**. *Tried and reverted*: a
87	   "replan only if path invalid" BT — real bug in this Nav2/Humble version
88	   (`IsPathValid` returns SUCCESS on an empty/uninitialized path before `ComputePathToPose` runs).
89	2. Slowed replan rate (1→0.2Hz) — partial help, but `allow_reversing:true` gave the controller a
90	   second degree of freedom to flip-flop on.
91	3. Real fix (for this specific symptom): `progress_checker` was aborting mid-maneuver —
92	   `SimpleProgressChecker` in this Humble version only judges linear displacement
93	   (`required_angular_distance` silently a no-op), so small heading-correction moves looked
94	   "stuck."
95	4. Workaround tried and rejected by user: loosen `yaw_goal_tolerance` to ~166°. User said heading
96	   precision genuinely matters — do not present this as the accepted fix.
97	5. **Real architectural fix**: switched global planner `NavfnPlanner` → `SmacPlannerHybrid` with
98	   Reeds-Shepp motion model. **This is the change that introduced K-turns/cusps into planned
99	   paths at all** — before this, per the user's own account (2026-08-31 message), planned paths
100	   were continuous, without direction reversals; an Ackermann vehicle can't always achieve every
101	   goal that way, so this was a necessary and correct change, but it created an entirely new
102	   class of problem (cusp handling) that hadn't existed before.
103	6. Re-applied the replan-rate slowdown now that `progress_checker` was patient.
104	7. **Discovered `RegulatedPurePursuitController` (RPP) cannot handle cusps at all** in this
105	   Nav2/Humble version — single lookahead "carrot point" goes unstable exactly at a
106	   direction-reversal point. Workaround: forced planner to forward-only Dubins paths (no cusps).
107	8. User **rejected** the forward-only workaround — reversing is a real requirement. Re-enabled
108	   reversing with much more conservative RPP tuning (tighter lookahead, slower approach to tight
109	   curvature).
110	9. **Still failed intermittently** even after (8)'s tuning — one goal 85s, a near-identical one
111	   7.6 minutes before giving up. Concluded this is RPP's inherent algorithmic limitation, not
112	   tunable. **Switched local controller to MPPI.**
113	
114	### MPPI did not immediately solve it either — more rounds followed, same day/next day
115	10. `enforce_path_inversion` was missing entirely — MPPI had no idea how to handle a cusp/reversal
116	    path at all after the switch.
117	11. `CostCritic.consider_footprint` silently defaulting to `false` — collision checked at robot
118	    center only, causing corner-cutting. Fixed, and replaced the costmap's circular
119	    `robot_radius: 0.15` approximation with a real rectangular footprint measured off the STL
120	    (`0.44m × 0.18m` — same number already used in the thesis's near-wall-tolerance section).
121	12. **First live-verified test in this whole thread** (previously relying on user-reported logs):
122	    a goal succeeded but not cleanly (0.202m/6.97° error); a second, harder goal **timed out
123	    completely** — same RPP-style failure signature reproduced even under MPPI. Isolated via live
124	    A/B param testing that `consider_footprint: true` (the correctness fix in (11)) is itself a
125	    real, understood trade-off — an accurate footprint is harder to keep collision-free in a tight
126	    K-turn than the old undersized circle was.
127	13. AMCL jitter tuning — measured live `map→odom` TF jumps up to 7.2cm/2.3°. Tuning helped the
128	    *character* of the jitter (more frequent, smaller corrections) but did **not** fix the
129	    underlying goal-reaching failures.
130	14. **A clean isolation test ruling out vehicle physics**: bypassed all of Nav2, published raw
131	    `/cmd_vel` directly, measured TF. Pure reverse: 2mm lateral drift. Reverse+steering together:
132	    smooth, monotonic, no instability. Proved the vehicle itself can execute a clean K-turn — the
133	    remaining failure was entirely in the Nav2 stack, not the robot.
134	15. Root cause found: `PreferForwardCritic` (penalizes reverse) vs. `PathFollowCritic` (stops
135	    enforcing the plan inside 1.4m of goal) left a 0.5m–1.4m "dead zone" where nothing enforced
136	    the plan but reverse motion was still actively penalized — exactly where a K-turn's reversal
137	    segment falls. Removed `PreferForwardCritic`, closed the dead zone. A previously
138	    catastrophically-failing goal (2.2m/177° error) converged to 0.145m/0.22°.
139	    **Still not presented as a complete fix even in the source material** — more issues followed.
140	
141	### Further issues specifically caused by the new K-turn/cusp paths (2026-07-18/19)
142	16. Four stacked bugs behind a goal still not succeeding:
143	    - A BT.CPP `Fallback`/`SingleTrigger` interaction silently re-armed a one-shot trigger,
144	      causing **33Hz continuous replanning**. Fixed by using a plain `<Sequence>` instead.
145	    - **Planner and controller shared the exact same minimum turning radius (0.5m) — zero
146	      margin.** Any MPPI sample noisier than perfect got penalized, so MPPI preferred staying
147	      still. Fixed by giving the planner more slack (0.7m) than the controller's true hard limit
148	      (0.5m). **This is the "increase the turning radius" step the user specifically
149	      recalled.**
150	    - MPPI's own warm-start (sampling noise around the *previous* cycle's control sequence) made
151	      a stall self-reinforcing once it collapsed toward zero velocity.
152	17. `EarlyCommitCritic` (built to fix a separate "robot doesn't turn at the start" problem) was
153	    found fighting legitimate reverse/K-turn segments — it assumed forward travel only, scoring a
154	    correct reverse maneuver as maximally wrong. Fixed with a direction-aware
155	    `min(fwd, reverse)` bearing distance. **Already reflected in the thesis's existing
156	    `EarlyCommitCritic` description in Ch6.**
157	18. 2026-07-20: `minimum_turning_radius` raised further, 0.7→1.0, paired with `yaw_goal_tolerance`
158	    0.3→0.5 — the last user-tuned accuracy fix visible in this cluster.
159	19. **2026-08-02, full detail (read directly from changelog)**: corner-cutting/path-deviation
160	    rigorously investigated on the user's own reported goal. Notably, **the investigation's first
161	    pass had its own bug** — comparing live position against a stale `/plan` snapshot instead of
162	    whichever plan was actually active at each timestamp, producing meaningless numbers; fixed by
163	    capturing every distinct plan snapshot with its own timestamp. With that fixed, measured a
164	    real, repeatable peak deviation of 0.44m at 60-70% through the maneuver, converging back to
165	    ~0.11-0.13m near the goal. Five parameters tested with an actual numeric harness (not
166	    impression): steering PID `kd`, `PathFollowCritic`/`PathAngleCritic.offset_from_furthest`
167	    (at two different values), `PathAlignCritic.cost_weight` (lowered this time, having only been
168	    raised before), `GoalAngleCritic.threshold_to_consider`, and `wz_std` alone — **none produced
169	    a change clearly beyond single-trial noise**. Synthesis: contrasted against a milder goal
170	    showing much smaller deviation, concluded the goal's own geometry (~180° heading change over
171	    ~2m net translation, close to the vehicle's kinematic limits) is the dominant driver, not any
172	    single tunable parameter — a genuine, evidence-based "this is a goal-shape-dependent
173	    limitation" conclusion, not an unexamined shrug.
174	
175	### Honest framing for the thesis (per user's correction, 2026-08-31)
176	This entire arc should NOT be written up as "problem → root cause → fixed." It should be written
177	as: switching to Reeds-Shepp path planning was necessary and correct (an Ackermann vehicle cannot
178	always reach a goal via a continuous, non-reversing path), but it introduced K-turns/cusps as an
179	entirely new class of problem that the existing controller (RPP) couldn't handle at all, motivating
180	the MPPI switch — which itself then needed multiple further rounds of fixes specifically because of
181	the new cusp-containing paths, and even after all of them, the user's own assessment is **"close to
182	perfect" but explicitly not a 100% fix**. This is consistent with — and a much richer version of —
183	the MPPI reversal-cusp-freeze work already in Ch6 (§sec:cusp-freeze), which picks up this same
184	thread later (2026-08-25 onward) with the dedicated `CuspStraightenerSmoother`. These two
185	investigations are the same underlying problem (K-turn/cusp handling) at two different points in
186	the project's timeline, and should probably be connected explicitly rather than presented as
187	unrelated.
188	
189	---
190	
191	## Phase 5b — More from `TUNING.md` (the project's own living cross-reference, checked 2026-08-31)
192	`TUNING.md` is a consolidated, cross-referenced summary the project kept up to date throughout —
193	it independently confirms everything in Phase 5 above and adds several items not yet captured:
194	
195	- **The project's own documentation contains an explicit self-correction.** `TUNING.md` §4
196	  literally says: *"Correction (2026-07-18 (6)/(7)): MPPI is not immune to this either. The line
197	  that used to be here claimed MPPI's trajectory-sampling approach doesn't share RPP's cusp
198	  failure mode — that turned out to be wrong, just live-verified too late to have caught it
199	  earlier."* This is direct, primary-source support for the user's point that this was never a
200	  clean, one-shot fix — even the project's own reference doc had to retract an earlier claim.
201	- **`GoalAngleCritic.cost_weight` raised 3.0→10.0 (2026-07-18 (5))** — fixes a *different* freeze:
202	  a goal that's mainly a reorientation (same/near position, new final yaw) wasn't moving at all.
203	  Root cause: `PathAlignCritic`/`PathFollowCritic`/`PathAngleCritic` all gate on distance from the
204	  robot's *current* pose to the goal, which is ~0 for this scenario from the first control cycle —
205	  disabling all three path-following critics for the entire maneuver, leaving only
206	  `GoalAngleCritic` active against `ConstraintCritic`'s turning-radius penalty. **Explicitly
207	  marked "not a complete fix"** even after the weight raise — still occasionally fails outright on
208	  retry-budget exhaustion, since MPPI's sampling is stochastic and the underlying critic-gating
209	  gap is unchanged. **This is the correct citation for the "final-goal reorientation freeze"
210	  already mentioned in Ch6's cusp-freeze section** (§sec:cusp-freeze) — I described this generically
211	  earlier in this session without a solid source; this is the real mechanism and it should be
212	  cited properly.
213	- **The mid-route cusp freeze (2026-07-18 (6)) is the same architectural issue as the later,
214	  fully-resolved cusp-freeze investigation already in Ch6.** `TUNING.md` names the exact same
215	  mechanism the thesis's existing §sec:cusp-freeze cites: `path_handler.cpp`'s
216	  `isWithinInversionTolerances()`, combined with `SmacPlannerHybrid` inserting a fresh small
217	  corrective reversal on nearly every replan. At the time `TUNING.md` was written (mid-July), this
218	  was **not yet fixed** — only properly root-caused and resolved with the dedicated
219	  `CuspStraightenerSmoother` over a month later (2026-08-25 onward). Strong confirmation these are
220	  the same underlying problem recurring at two points in the project's timeline, not two separate
221	  bugs — Ch6 should probably say so explicitly.
222	- **A statistical-rigor lesson (2026-07-19 (3))**: investigated raising `PathAlignCritic.cost_weight`
223	  to fix corner-cutting. Tried `14.0` (worse — overshot the other way) and `12.0` (same overshoot,
224	  not a graded response). A repeat run at the *default* `10.0` swung even wider on a different run
225	  of the identical goal — concluded MPPI's run-to-run stochasticity is large enough that a
226	  single-run weight experiment isn't reliable evidence, and deliberately left the parameter at
227	  default rather than commit to an untested value pending a proper multi-trial comparison. Good,
228	  honest example of recognizing insufficient evidence rather than shipping a plausible-looking fix.
229	- **`batch_size` raised 2000→2500/3500 (2026-07-19 (4))** — a genuine "real improvement, real cost"
230	  story: measurably fixed path-tracking looseness (p90 deviation `0.33-0.41m → 0.25-0.26m`,
231	  reproducible across trials) but degraded control-loop timing enough near the goal that one
232	  otherwise-normal run took **4.5 minutes** to converge instead of ~30s. Reverted for that cost,
233	  not because the fix didn't work.
234	- **The original cusp-freeze discovery, in full (2026-07-18 (6)), read directly from the
235	  changelog**: user reported the robot getting stuck on a path with a reversal-then-forward
236	  segment. Reproduced live on the same K-turn benchmark goal `(2.0, 1.0, 179°)` used throughout
237	  this arc — repeated `Failed to make progress` → abort → recovery → full replan, never reaching
238	  the goal across multiple 60-150s+ attempts. Ruled out as a regression from the same day's other
239	  fixes (reverted them live, reproduced identically). Root cause candidate identified — the exact
240	  same mechanism as Ch6's already-resolved investigation: `path_handler.cpp`'s
241	  `isWithinInversionTolerances()` requires satisfying both an xy and yaw tolerance at a cusp
242	  simultaneously before the rest of the path is released, and `SmacPlannerHybrid` was frequently
243	  inserting a *new* small corrective reversal at the start of nearly every fresh replan, each too
244	  short to satisfy `progress_checker`'s movement-time allowance, triggering another abort/replan
245	  cycle. Loosening the inversion tolerances live helped (more net progress per attempt) but did
246	  **not reliably fix it** within the test budget. **The user explicitly chose to pause the
247	  investigation here rather than keep iterating live** — it was deliberately left open, not
248	  abandoned by neglect. This is the true starting point of the cusp-freeze story: first found and
249	  clearly diagnosed 2026-07-18, left unresolved for over a month, then properly root-caused and
250	  fixed via the dedicated `CuspStraightenerSmoother` starting 2026-08-25. Ch6 should reflect this
251	  real timeline rather than presenting the August work as the start of the investigation.
252	- **A related, only-partially-resolved fix (2026-07-18 (7))**: fixed a narrower symptom — the
253	  robot not moving at all when the path's *first* segment needs a turn the start heading doesn't
254	  match. Root cause: `SmacPlannerHybrid`'s `change_penalty` defaulted to `0.0` (Nav2's real
255	  default, not a misconfiguration), so the planner had zero cost for inserting an unnecessary
256	  reversal as literally the first segment of a path. Fixed by raising it to `3.0`. **This surfaced
257	  a new trade-off, not fully resolved**: for large heading-change goals, the raised
258	  `change_penalty` combined with the already-raised `reverse_penalty` now sometimes pushes the
259	  planner toward a long forward-only loop instead of a short reverse — on the live test run, the
260	  robot followed the loop several meters past the goal, then stalled rotating in place for tens of
261	  seconds before the test was stopped. Explicitly flagged as the same underlying tension as the
262	  (6) freeze above: `reverse_penalty`/`change_penalty` discourage exactly the reversal/direction-change
263	  behavior this vehicle sometimes genuinely needs.
264	- **AMCL's `DifferentialMotionModel` confirmed correct for this Ackermann vehicle, not a bug** —
265	  checked directly against the Nav2 source; "Differential" here refers to how odometry noise is
266	  decomposed (rotate-translate-rotate), not the drivetrain type, and is the right choice for any
267	  non-holonomic robot, car-like or not. Nothing to fix, but worth a sentence confirming this was
268	  checked rather than assumed.
269	
270	## Open correction (found 2026-08-30, not yet applied to thesis)
271	Ch6's already-written "curvature-continuing" cusp-extension refinement (added earlier this
272	session) describes a two-point curvature estimate that the changelog shows was buggy — it made
273	the extension curve too tightly and the robot deviated off-path. Fixed 2026-08-29 (same day) by
274	averaging curvature over a ~0.15m lookback window instead. The thesis currently describes the
275	buggy version. **Needs correction before this section is considered final.**
276	
277	**CONFIRMED by `TUNING.md`/`PARAMS_REFERENCE.md`, both freshly rewritten 2026-08-31** (the user
278	updated these project files directly): the correction above is exactly right — both files now
279	state the windowed-curvature version explicitly and both say plainly, in so many words, **"not
280	yet hardware-tested"** for the curvature-continuing extension AND for `min_lead_distance`
281	(also added 2026-08-29). Ch6 must not present either refinement as validated beyond simulation.
282	
283	## Phase 5c — `TUNING.md`/`PARAMS_REFERENCE.md` refreshed 2026-08-31 (user's own maintenance pass)
284	The user directly rewrote these two files today, catching drift between the docs and the live
285	config. Confirms everything in Phase 5/5b and adds:
286	
287	- **§2a (`cusp_straightener`) is now written up authoritatively as "RESOLVED 2026-08-26"** for the
288	  mid-route cusp freeze, with the full trial numbers: baseline 110.2s/2 recoveries →
289	  `straight_distance` alone 86.7s/1.3 → `straight_distance`+`extend_distance` 43.9s/0 (final
290	  locked-in config, hardware-validated 2/2 goals, 0 recoveries). Explicitly states widening
291	  `inversion_xy_tolerance`/`inversion_yaw_tolerance` was tried again on 2026-08-25 and was
292	  **worse** (aborts before even reaching the cusp) — the smoother is what actually worked, not
293	  loosening MPPI's own gating.
294	- **A genuinely new, currently open, unresolved discrepancy in the live codebase**:
295	  `PathFollowCritic`/`PathAngleCritic.offset_from_furthest` was lowered from defaults (6/4) to
296	  (3/2) on 2026-07-18 to fix a "turning early" bug — but the live config is **currently back at
297	  the defaults (6/4)**, and no changelog entry documents when or why it was reverted. The user's
298	  own fresh audit flags this explicitly: *"treat this as a real, currently-unexplained discrepancy
299	  ... re-verify against the original 'turning early' symptom before trusting either value
300	  blindly."* **Do not present the "turning early" fix as a settled, currently-active fix in the
301	  thesis** — the value that supposedly fixed it is not actually deployed right now, for reasons
302	  nobody has recorded.
303	- The near-wall goal / `tolerance` silent-wrong-pose story (already accurately in Ch6) is now
304	  independently confirmed word-for-word in the project's own reference doc, including the same
305	  citation to the "prefer visible failure" project principle already used in Ch6.
306	- Minor: `max_planning_time` (5.0s) confirmed live (2026-08-29) to never actually be the limiting
307	  factor on a hard/infeasible goal — `max_iterations` is what's hit first (each failed attempt
308	  2.5-3.6s, well under the time cap).
309	
310	---
311	
312	## Coverage status (as of 2026-08-31)
313	All three CHANGELOG.md files (`qcar_initial`, `qcar_ackermann`, `qcar_updated`) now fully read —
314	confirmed `qcar_initial`/`qcar_ackermann` are identical copies of `qcar_updated`'s history up to
315	their respective rename points, no unique content. `TUNING.md` and a sample of
316	`PARAMS_REFERENCE.md` also read (the latter is a dry parameter reference with no unique
317	narrative beyond `TUNING.md`). All memory files read. `qcar_navigation` has no separate
318	CHANGELOG.md — its only history is the memory files already covered. Git log fully reviewed.
319	All 8 status PPTs and 3 chat summaries reviewed.
320	
321	**This is believed to be complete coverage of the available written history.** Remaining
322	uncertainty is only in the user's own recollection of anything not captured in any of these
323	artifacts.

# Project History — Working Findings Document

**Status: DRAFT / staging area. Not part of the compiled thesis. Nothing here has been
merged into the `.tex` chapters yet — this is a running log while we reconstruct the full
project history from git, changelogs, memory, status PPTs, and chat summaries, before deciding
what goes into the report and how.**

Sources consulted so far: git log (`qcar_hardware` repo), `qcar_initial`/`qcar_ackermann`/
`qcar_updated` CHANGELOG.md files, `qcar_navigation` memory, 8 status PPTs (2026-04-27 to
2026-08-17), 3 chat summaries (chat-till-June-17, a parallel qcar_ackermann chat, and this
conversation's own MPPI cusp-freeze work).

Package lineage: `qcar_initial` (baseline) → `qcar_ackermann` (throwaway test package for the
Ackermann-plugin prototype, merged back) → renamed to `qcar_updated` (final package).

---

## Phase 0 — Planning (2026-04-27)
- Scoped: ROS2 SLAM+Nav2 for QCar, originally including EKF/UKF sensor fusion (dropped later,
  never implemented — replaced by dead-reckoning odometry).
- Started on ROS 2 Foxy in Docker; not yet Humble.

## Phase 1 — ROS 2 Humble bring-up (~early May, PPT 2026-05-11)
- Upgraded to Ubuntu 22.04 + ROS 2 Humble natively.
- URDF (received, not built from scratch) adapted: transmission tags, D435 camera macro, control
  plugin fixed for ROS2 compatibility.
- First working Gazebo spawn + RViz with correct TF + `ros2_control` stack + teleop.
- **Status: not in thesis at all** — the whole foundational bring-up chapter.

## Phase 2 — First SLAM attempts, `qcar_initial` (mid-May – early June)
- Earlier `diff_drive_controller` attempt abandoned (wheel-orientation conflicts from
  `rpy="0 0 3.14"`) → settled on JointGroup controllers + `cmd_vel_to_drive.py` (= thesis's
  current "Baseline" section).
- PPT 2026-05-25: LiDAR + Cartographer added, first map built. **Issue**: "Robot orientation not
  updating in RViz" — root cause named as QoS mismatch between `joint_state_broadcaster` and
  `robot_state_publisher`.
- PPT 2026-06-08: Nav2 launched (imprecise). **Issue**: robot pose static in RViz while moving in
  Gazebo — refined root cause: missing odom→base transform, since `drive_controller` never
  published odometry.
- **Status: partially in thesis** (end-state ground-truth-odom decision is in §3.2; the TF
  debugging itself is not narrated).

## Phase 3 — `qcar_ackermann`: prototyping the Ackermann plugin (mid-June)
Built as a throwaway test package to prove dropping `ros2_control` for
`libgazebo_ros_ackermann_drive`, later merged back into `qcar_initial`. Bug chain, from the
chat-till-June-17 + parallel qcar_ackermann chat:
- Launch bugs: `robot_description` YAML parse error (`Command()` not typed as string), unreliable
  Gazebo launch pattern, spawn race condition.
- False lead: "robot spawned without wheels" — actually LiDAR ray-visualization obscuring the
  view, not a real defect.
- Dual actuation conflict — old and new drive plugins both active, fighting over `/cmd_vel`.
- Ackermann joint-mapping bug — wrong joint names, steering silently ignored.
- **LiDAR TF bug** — `continuous` joint with no `/joint_states` source, blocked all of Nav2.

## Phase 5 — The goal-approach oscillation → planner/controller saga (2026-07-14, all one day)
**This is NOT a clean one-shot fix. It's an iterative arc that changed both the planner and the
controller, and even after 9+ rounds was not claimed as fully solved. Document it as an ongoing,
partially-resolved investigation, not a solved bug.**

Starting symptom: robot reaches goal position but swings/wobbles correcting final orientation.

1. Root cause: `NavfnPlanner` has no heading concept at all; default BT replans every second
   continuously, even after reaching goal position. Removed `<Spin>` recovery (physically
   impossible for this car) — **already in thesis, §sec:bt-fix**. *Tried and reverted*: a
   "replan only if path invalid" BT — real bug in this Nav2/Humble version
   (`IsPathValid` returns SUCCESS on an empty/uninitialized path before `ComputePathToPose` runs).
2. Slowed replan rate (1→0.2Hz) — partial help, but `allow_reversing:true` gave the controller a
   second degree of freedom to flip-flop on.
3. Real fix (for this specific symptom): `progress_checker` was aborting mid-maneuver —
   `SimpleProgressChecker` in this Humble version only judges linear displacement
   (`required_angular_distance` silently a no-op), so small heading-correction moves looked
   "stuck."
4. Workaround tried and rejected by user: loosen `yaw_goal_tolerance` to ~166°. User said heading
   precision genuinely matters — do not present this as the accepted fix.
5. **Real architectural fix**: switched global planner `NavfnPlanner` → `SmacPlannerHybrid` with
   Reeds-Shepp motion model. **This is the change that introduced K-turns/cusps into planned
   paths at all** — before this, per the user's own account (2026-08-31 message), planned paths
   were continuous, without direction reversals; an Ackermann vehicle can't always achieve every
   goal that way, so this was a necessary and correct change, but it created an entirely new
   class of problem (cusp handling) that hadn't existed before.
6. Re-applied the replan-rate slowdown now that `progress_checker` was patient.
7. **Discovered `RegulatedPurePursuitController` (RPP) cannot handle cusps at all** in this
   Nav2/Humble version — single lookahead "carrot point" goes unstable exactly at a
   direction-reversal point. Workaround: forced planner to forward-only Dubins paths (no cusps).
8. User **rejected** the forward-only workaround — reversing is a real requirement. Re-enabled
   reversing with much more conservative RPP tuning (tighter lookahead, slower approach to tight
   curvature).
9. **Still failed intermittently** even after (8)'s tuning — one goal 85s, a near-identical one
   7.6 minutes before giving up. Concluded this is RPP's inherent algorithmic limitation, not
   tunable. **Switched local controller to MPPI.**

### MPPI did not immediately solve it either — more rounds followed, same day/next day
10. `enforce_path_inversion` was missing entirely — MPPI had no idea how to handle a cusp/reversal
    path at all after the switch.
11. `CostCritic.consider_footprint` silently defaulting to `false` — collision checked at robot
    center only, causing corner-cutting. Fixed, and replaced the costmap's circular
    `robot_radius: 0.15` approximation with a real rectangular footprint measured off the STL
    (`0.44m × 0.18m` — same number already used in the thesis's near-wall-tolerance section).
12. **First live-verified test in this whole thread** (previously relying on user-reported logs):
    a goal succeeded but not cleanly (0.202m/6.97° error); a second, harder goal **timed out
    completely** — same RPP-style failure signature reproduced even under MPPI. Isolated via live
    A/B param testing that `consider_footprint: true` (the correctness fix in (11)) is itself a
    real, understood trade-off — an accurate footprint is harder to keep collision-free in a tight
    K-turn than the old undersized circle was.
13. AMCL jitter tuning — measured live `map→odom` TF jumps up to 7.2cm/2.3°. Tuning helped the
    *character* of the jitter (more frequent, smaller corrections) but did **not** fix the
    underlying goal-reaching failures.
14. **A clean isolation test ruling out vehicle physics**: bypassed all of Nav2, published raw
    `/cmd_vel` directly, measured TF. Pure reverse: 2mm lateral drift. Reverse+steering together:
    smooth, monotonic, no instability. Proved the vehicle itself can execute a clean K-turn — the
    remaining failure was entirely in the Nav2 stack, not the robot.
15. Root cause found: `PreferForwardCritic` (penalizes reverse) vs. `PathFollowCritic` (stops
    enforcing the plan inside 1.4m of goal) left a 0.5m–1.4m "dead zone" where nothing enforced
    the plan but reverse motion was still actively penalized — exactly where a K-turn's reversal
    segment falls. Removed `PreferForwardCritic`, closed the dead zone. A previously
    catastrophically-failing goal (2.2m/177° error) converged to 0.145m/0.22°.
    **Still not presented as a complete fix even in the source material** — more issues followed.

### Further issues specifically caused by the new K-turn/cusp paths (2026-07-18/19)
16. Four stacked bugs behind a goal still not succeeding:
    - A BT.CPP `Fallback`/`SingleTrigger` interaction silently re-armed a one-shot trigger,
      causing **33Hz continuous replanning**. Fixed by using a plain `<Sequence>` instead.
    - **Planner and controller shared the exact same minimum turning radius (0.5m) — zero
      margin.** Any MPPI sample noisier than perfect got penalized, so MPPI preferred staying
      still. Fixed by giving the planner more slack (0.7m) than the controller's true hard limit
      (0.5m). **This is the "increase the turning radius" step the user specifically
      recalled.**
    - MPPI's own warm-start (sampling noise around the *previous* cycle's control sequence) made
      a stall self-reinforcing once it collapsed toward zero velocity.
17. `EarlyCommitCritic` (built to fix a separate "robot doesn't turn at the start" problem) was
    found fighting legitimate reverse/K-turn segments — it assumed forward travel only, scoring a
    correct reverse maneuver as maximally wrong. Fixed with a direction-aware
    `min(fwd, reverse)` bearing distance. **Already reflected in the thesis's existing
    `EarlyCommitCritic` description in Ch6.**
18. 2026-07-20: `minimum_turning_radius` raised further, 0.7→1.0, paired with `yaw_goal_tolerance`
    0.3→0.5 — the last user-tuned accuracy fix visible in this cluster.
19. **2026-08-02, full detail (read directly from changelog)**: corner-cutting/path-deviation
    rigorously investigated on the user's own reported goal. Notably, **the investigation's first
    pass had its own bug** — comparing live position against a stale `/plan` snapshot instead of
    whichever plan was actually active at each timestamp, producing meaningless numbers; fixed by
    capturing every distinct plan snapshot with its own timestamp. With that fixed, measured a
    real, repeatable peak deviation of 0.44m at 60-70% through the maneuver, converging back to
    ~0.11-0.13m near the goal. Five parameters tested with an actual numeric harness (not
    impression): steering PID `kd`, `PathFollowCritic`/`PathAngleCritic.offset_from_furthest`
    (at two different values), `PathAlignCritic.cost_weight` (lowered this time, having only been
    raised before), `GoalAngleCritic.threshold_to_consider`, and `wz_std` alone — **none produced
    a change clearly beyond single-trial noise**. Synthesis: contrasted against a milder goal
    showing much smaller deviation, concluded the goal's own geometry (~180° heading change over
    ~2m net translation, close to the vehicle's kinematic limits) is the dominant driver, not any
    single tunable parameter — a genuine, evidence-based "this is a goal-shape-dependent
    limitation" conclusion, not an unexamined shrug.

### Honest framing for the thesis (per user's correction, 2026-08-31)
This entire arc should NOT be written up as "problem → root cause → fixed." It should be written
as: switching to Reeds-Shepp path planning was necessary and correct (an Ackermann vehicle cannot
always reach a goal via a continuous, non-reversing path), but it introduced K-turns/cusps as an
entirely new class of problem that the existing controller (RPP) couldn't handle at all, motivating
the MPPI switch — which itself then needed multiple further rounds of fixes specifically because of
the new cusp-containing paths, and even after all of them, the user's own assessment is **"close to
perfect" but explicitly not a 100% fix**. This is consistent with — and a much richer version of —
the MPPI reversal-cusp-freeze work already in Ch6 (§sec:cusp-freeze), which picks up this same
thread later (2026-08-25 onward) with the dedicated `CuspStraightenerSmoother`. These two
investigations are the same underlying problem (K-turn/cusp handling) at two different points in
the project's timeline, and should probably be connected explicitly rather than presented as
unrelated.

% Abstract - guideline 4.1.6: optional, 120-150 words recommended,
% describes the problem and results, with key words.

\chapter*{Abstract}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{Abstract}

% TODO: this draft is ~150 words; trim or adjust once the final
% results chapter numbers are locked in, and re-check the word count.

Autonomous mobile robots are typically developed in simulation before
being deployed on physical hardware, yet the transfer from simulator to
real platform routinely exposes gaps that no amount of simulated
testing predicts. This thesis documents the end-to-end migration of a
ROS~2 Nav2 navigation stack for an Ackermann-steered vehicle, the
Quanser QCar, from a Gazebo simulation onto the physical robot. A
protocol-level incompatibility between the robot's onboard ROS~2
Dashing distribution and a ROS~2 Humble development host made native
ROS~2 communication impossible, motivating a custom TCP/JSON bridge.
The thesis presents the bridge's design, the calibration of an
open-loop throttle model against real actuator behaviour, and the
root-cause diagnosis of a hardware abstraction-layer buffering defect
that had been misattributed to physical drivetrain coasting. The
resulting system is validated through closed-loop Nav2 goal-reaching
tests on the physical vehicle, and the observed sim-to-real
discrepancies are quantified and discussed.

\vspace{0.5cm}
\noindent\textbf{Key words:} ROS~2, Nav2, Ackermann steering, sim-to-real
transfer, Gazebo, Model Predictive Path Integral control, mobile robot
navigation, Quanser QCar

\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python,caption={The one-line HAL construction change that fixed the buffering defect (\texttt{qcar\_bridge.py}).},label={lst:readmode-fix}]
# readMode=0 (immediate I/O) - was 1 (task-based I/O), which runs a
# background acquisition task into a 100-sample ring buffer
# (frequency*2) from the moment this object is constructed,
# independent of when car.read() actually starts being called. Since
# this object is created before the listening socket even opens, and
# car.read() isn't called until a relay connects, the buffer fills and
# starts overwriting during that gap - once reads begin at the matched
# 50Hz rate, they get permanently stuck ~100 samples (~2.0s) behind
# real-time, since the backlog never drains. Immediate I/O reads
# current hardware state directly, no task/buffer involved.
car = QCar(readMode=0, frequency=READ_RATE)
\end{lstlisting}

# residual speed when a stop is commanded) to counter drivetrain coast -
